inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 reported revenue 6,497.2 less ~215 of Digital Markets ('Other' segment, sold to G2 in Feb 2026; Q2 2025 Other revenue was 55.9). Pro forma continuing base so that FY2026 guidance (>=6,375) is a like-for-like year-1 growth of ~1.5%.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-06-30: 163,602,067 issued less 99,197,399 treasury = 64.40M outstanding (Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet), plus ~0.1M dilutive awards (Q2 2026 diluted 66.6M vs basic 66.5M weighted). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The 2026-07-31 cover count of 63.15M is lower only because July repurchases were funded from the June cash balance; pairing it with the June balance sheet would count that cash twice.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Company definition (OCF 1,290.4 less capex 115.1, FY2025). Company FY2026 guidance is FCF >= 1,185.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income was 64.7 but Gartner is a net-debt company (net debt 1,491 at 2026-06-30), so no cash pile is added to EV and the income is NOT stripped from the FCF base.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement add-back (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation 155,877k). Gartner publishes no combined 'SBC incl. equity-award taxes' line; shares withheld for taxes on RSU vesting are settled inside 'Purchases of treasury stock' and are not separately tagged, so they cannot be isolated and are not added. SBC is therefore understated by an unquantified low-tens-of-millions per year.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchases of treasury stock 1,991.1; H1-2026 1,081.8 (Q2 2026 alone 547.1, 3.6M shares). Repurchaser: the flat count is funded, not a modelling convention. Board added $500M to the authorisation in July 2026.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. 10y UST ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.2 (post-Feb-2026 volatility) -> cost of equity ~10.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% on $3.0B of senior notes (4.2% after tax). Market-value weights ~80/20 equity/debt -> WACC ~9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; risk is charged once, through the scenario weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (ASC 842) stay inside EBITDA as rent expense (operating lease cost 88.0 in FY2025), so the lease cost is already in the flows. Operating lease liability (350.2 at 2026-06-30) is NOT added to net debt. One treatment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year explicit horizon, via .claude/skills/dcf-methods routing (US operating company: subscription research/advisory). Mid-cycle normalisation NOT applied to margins: adjusted EBITDA margin is ~24.5% at both the FY2025 trough and in FY2026 guidance (>=1,570 on >=6,375), inside the FY2019-24 range, so margins are already normal. What broke is growth (Contract Value +1.7% FX-neutral YoY at Q2 2026 vs ~7-8% through 2024 and the withdrawn 12-16% algorithm), so the judgment sits in the growth paths: neither the 8% revenue history nor the ~1.5% trough is extrapolated. TIMING: valuation date is late Sept 2026 while the model's year 1 is the full FY2026; the June-30 balance sheet and share count already embed H1-2026 cash generation (H1 buybacks of 1,082 were funded by it), so H1-2026 owner FCF (662) is deducted in the equity bridge rather than double-counted. End-of-year discounting of flows that arrive ~9 months earlier than modelled remains a conservative offset that is left in place. First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF.

equity_bridge.item: Less H1-2026 owner FCF already embedded in the 30-Jun-2026 net debt and share count
equity_bridge.note: H1-2026 OCF 789.3 less capex 40.3 less SBC 86.9 (Q2 2026 10-Q). The model's year 1 is the full FY2026; the June balance sheet already absorbed this half-year's cash (funding the 1,081.8 of H1 buybacks), so it is removed here to avoid counting it twice.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Guidance-anchored base path (average of the first five base-case years). Equity CAGR is unusable: book equity fell from 1,090 (FY2020) to 320 (FY2025) and -167 (Q2 2026) because buybacks exceed earnings, not because the business shrank.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative and meaningless (buyback-driven) while revenue compounds at 6-10%; the FCF series, not book value, anchors the model.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs to FY2025. Revenue: FY2022 5,475.8 / FY2020 4,099.4 -> FY2025 6,497.2. EPS: FY2022 10.08 / FY2020 2.99 -> FY2025 9.68 (FY2025 carries a $150M non-deductible goodwill impairment; FY2020 was pandemic-depressed, so both EPS CAGRs are distorted). Owner FCF (OCF - capex - SBC; interest income not stripped because net debt is positive): FY2020 756.8, FY2021 1,154.1, FY2022 902.8, FY2023 922.8, FY2024 1,228.4, FY2025 1,019.3. Owner-FCF CAGRs (4.1% / 6.1%) run ~1.5pp below reported-FCF CAGRs (5.8% / 7.5%): SBC grew from 62.6 to 155.9 over five years, faster than cash flow, so a rising share of reported growth was paid for in stock. FY2024 FCF was flattered by a 122 deferred-revenue inflow that reversed (-42) in FY2025 as CV stalled.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 = FY2026 guidance (>=6,375 on a 6,282 pro forma base). Revenue lags Contract Value by 2-3 quarters; CV was +1.7% FX-neutral YoY at Q2 2026 and accelerating sequentially, so FY2027 is mid-single-digit at best (3.5%) and the path peaks at 5.5% in FY2029-30 - roughly two-thirds of the 2024 run-rate, never the 12-16% algorithm. Decelerates to 3% by year 10.
base.margin_rationale: 24.6% = FY2026 guided adjusted EBITDA (>=1,570) on guided revenue (>=6,375); FY2025 pro forma ex-Digital Markets was ~24.5%. Rises 190bp over ten years to 26.5% as sales-force productivity recovers on a fixed research-content base; FY2021-22 reached 25-26% with pandemic cost relief, so 26.5% is modest operating leverage, not a new peak.
base.sbc_rationale: FY2025 2.4% of revenue, H1-2026 2.7%, FY2024 2.5%. Held near 2.5% and eased to 2.3% only late.
base.da_rationale: FY2025 D&A 200.3 (3.1%) includes ~80/yr amortisation of CEB-acquisition intangibles that runs off; H1-2026 was 2.8%. Glides to 1.8%, roughly equal to capex, by year 7.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid / pre-tax income: FY2023 26.7%, FY2024 22.6%, FY2025 18.7% on impairment-adjusted pre-tax (209.6 / 1,118); H1-2026 GAAP provision 23.1%. 22% in year 1 then 23%.
base.wc_rationale: Prepaid annual subscriptions: deferred revenue is ~43% of revenue and fees receivable ~23%, so net working capital releases ~20 cents per dollar of revenue growth. Modelled on the CHANGE in revenue; the FY2024 122 inflow reversed to -42 in FY2025 when CV stalled, which is exactly why it is not a fixed share of revenue.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 2.5% growth vs an 18x owner-FCF cap; the engine takes the lower.

bull.growth_rationale: CV reaccelerates to high-single digits by FY2028-30 (AI-vendor-selection demand, restored sales productivity, federal book lapping DOGE cuts, Conferences sustaining double-digit growth); revenue follows to 8.5% - still below the 2024 CV run-rate plus price, and well short of the withdrawn 12-16% algorithm.
bull.margin_rationale: Operating leverage on a largely fixed research base takes adjusted EBITDA to 28% by year 6; FY2021 delivered 26% while growing 15%.

bear.growth_rationale: GenAI substitution of lower-tier research is structural: CV stalls at 0-2%, Consulting keeps shrinking, price increases are absorbed by seat attrition. Revenue grows ~1-2% - roughly inflation - for a decade.
bear.margin_rationale: Pricing power erodes while the analyst and sales base cannot be cut in step; adjusted EBITDA margin drifts to 22%, the low end of the FY2018-19 post-CEB range. Litigation cost and a possible class-action settlement sit inside the margin, not as a separate bridge item.

scenario_narratives.base: Contract Value growth recovers from the ~1-2% FY2025 trough to mid-single digits over FY2027-29 as elongated enterprise buying cycles normalise, AI-related research demand offsets GenAI substitution at the low end, and the federal book laps the DOGE-related cuts - but the 12-16% algorithm is not reinstated and revenue never exceeds 5.5% growth. Adjusted EBITDA margin expands ~190bp over ten years on sales productivity, capex stays ~1.7% of revenue, and the flat 64.5M share count is funded by ~$1B/yr of buybacks that are value-neutral in this model. Securities litigation is a cost and a distraction, not a solvency event.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Q2 2026 sequential CV acceleration proves durable: enterprises need vendor-neutral guidance on AI vendor selection, pricing and risk, Conferences sustain double-digit growth, and the restructured Insights organisation restores new-business productivity. CV reaches high-single digits by FY2028, revenue growth peaks at 8.5%, and operating leverage lifts adjusted EBITDA to 28%. The de-rated multiple (~8.6x EV/EBITDA, ~13x adjusted EPS at the current price) re-rates as the growth algorithm is visibly rebuilt.
scenario_narratives.bear: GenAI disintermediation is structural, not cyclical: LLM tools absorb the market-synthesis work that justified lower-tier subscriptions, seat counts shrink at renewal, and Consulting continues its decline. CV growth stays at 0-2%, the sales force cannot be resized quickly enough, and margins drift down to 22%. The class actions settle for a meaningful sum and management's credibility does not recover, so the terminal multiple is capped at 14x owner FCF.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30% because the whole thesis rests on an unproven reacceleration of a KPI that management mis-forecast badly enough to attract securities litigation, and because the GenAI substitution risk to the core Insights product is a live structural question, not a cyclical one. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right - CV back to high-single digits, margin expansion to 28%, and AI-advisory demand outrunning AI substitution. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Gartner is a high-margin, prepaid-subscription research franchise whose growth algorithm broke in 2025 and whose stock has been re-priced to a ~10% company-defined FCF yield. The valuation treats margins as already normal (no mid-cycle adjustment) and puts the entire judgment into the Contract Value recovery path, weighting the structural-erosion bear case at 30%. SBC is fully expensed and the share count held flat; buybacks are value-neutral. The market price sits close to the bear-case value, so the stock is only cheap if CV reacceleration is real.
key_risks_to_valuation: Contract Value growth fails to reaccelerate beyond ~2%: the base case assumes 5-5.5% revenue growth by FY2029, which needs CV back to mid-single digits.
GenAI substitution of lower-tier research proves structural, compressing seats and pricing power (the bear axis).
Consulting segment continues to decline (-8.8% YoY in Q2 2026) faster than Conferences can offset.
Securities class actions and fiduciary-duty investigations: settlement cost and management distraction; a large settlement would be a direct equity deduction not modelled as a bridge item.
Buyback pace (~$1B+ per half-year) exceeds FCF and is being funded from cash; if CV disappoints again, leverage rises against a shrinking EBITDA base.
SBC is understated: equity-award withholding taxes are settled inside treasury purchases and cannot be isolated from the filings.
Timing: end-of-year discounting of a full FY2026 year 1 from a late-September valuation date, offset by the H1-2026 bridge deduction; the net effect is mildly conservative.
